dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.prototype: R-3m four-site alternating Sc-C-Mo-C layered carbide; Sc and Mo have distinct single-site roles and C has a two-site orbit
candidate.prototype_evidence: R-3m four-site alternating Sc-C-Mo-C layered carbide; Sc and Mo have distinct single-site roles and C has a two-site orbit
candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: The original 2023 primary study associates appreciable coupling with an acoustic softening along Gamma-X and places predicted ScMoC2 49 meV/atom above its hull. This is a metastable research route, not equilibrium synthesis certification. Its later exact-source path has no signed negative printed modes and Gamma optical compression is positive; fine force .00823 eV/A and anisotropic stress .363 GPa remain finite-grid stationarity limits.
candidate.ambient_scope: Coarse/fine SCF both converge; complete source forces/stress, positive Gamma optical compression and no signed negative finite-path value support this model near ambient. All listed q outputs end JOBDONE/response convergence with zero routine errors. This is finite-grid local/metastable evidence, not exhaustive thermodynamic or all-irrep certification.
candidate.route_response: Replace W by Mo in the frozen ScWC2 analogue. Volume changes −0.342810%, Sc-C nearest distance −0.00476510 A and C-C +0.00726968 A. The same 4x4x4 PH grid with 13 q representatives yields all-ten lambda gains 10.495–13.659%; separate Eli mu=.1 increases 11.083→15.678 K. Tiny geometry changes accompany a chemically different metal response, so this is a coupled cation-construction hypothesis, not a geometry-only strain mechanism.
candidate.next_action: Test one common-grid acoustic Gamma-X/q-mode response in ScWC2 and ScMoC2, or an equal-volume composition cross-control. Favorable: the bounded Mo advantage persists with finite positive curvature; adverse: stronger softening turns the branch unstable or a competing decomposition route reverses near-ambient feasibility.

seven_criteria.identity: Raw CIF, literal coarse/fine crystal input and Gamma header agree by complete ordered species/site periodic association; exact natural-isotope discrete computational occupancy is export convention, experimental occupancy/P/T unknown. Source model configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC by exact-version defaults plus literal omission; magnetic ground state and binary build not certified.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Replace W by Mo in the frozen ScWC2 analogue. Volume changes −0.342810%, Sc-C nearest distance −0.00476510 A and C-C +0.00726968 A. The same 4x4x4 PH grid with 13 q representatives yields all-ten lambda gains 10.495–13.659%; separate Eli mu=.1 increases 11.083→15.678 K. Tiny geometry changes accompany a chemically different metal response, so this is a coupled cation-construction hypothesis, not a geometry-only strain mechanism.
seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Direct exact-source lambda has the favorable sign at all ten matched sigma tokens, independently accompanied by the separate mu=.1 Eli table. Finite-grid broadening sensitivity is preserved; differing PP/cutoff/version are model confounds where shown. Sigma units, physical error bar, fullBZ convergence and experimental Tc remain unknown.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Coarse/fine SCF both converge; complete source forces/stress, positive Gamma optical compression and no signed negative finite-path value support this model near ambient. All listed q outputs end JOBDONE/response convergence with zero routine errors. This is finite-grid local/metastable evidence, not exhaustive thermodynamic or all-irrep certification.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: The original 2023 primary study associates appreciable coupling with an acoustic softening along Gamma-X and places predicted ScMoC2 49 meV/atom above its hull. This is a metastable research route, not equilibrium synthesis certification. Its later exact-source path has no signed negative printed modes and Gamma optical compression is positive; fine force .00823 eV/A and anisotropic stress .363 GPa remain finite-grid stationarity limits.
seven_criteria.novelty: ScMoC2 was already predicted in the 2023 institutional primary paper (SG166); no first-discovery claim. A dated exact ScMoC2 superconductivity search found that prediction, not an experimental SC benchmark. The exact source phase and new matched W→Mo mechanism define the reviewed-catalogue candidate. The old paper hull/elastic calculation is separate-method supporting prior and is not silently assigned as a new exact-state measurement.
seven_criteria.decision: Test one common-grid acoustic Gamma-X/q-mode response in ScWC2 and ScMoC2, or an equal-volume composition cross-control. Favorable: the bounded Mo advantage persists with finite positive curvature; adverse: stronger softening turns the branch unstable or a competing decomposition route reverses near-ambient feasibility.
